**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 66–68 — the deliberate-restatement license**
> *"**This clause OWNS the consent gate. It is deliberately restated at the dispatch gate and THE COUNCIL: a reflex wants redundancy, and the Amendment Law prefers the rule that leaves a trace.**"*

EVIDENCE: It cites the **Amendment Law, which was deleted today** — it is prose supporting something already gone. The consent gate is now stated **six** times: Part I §2 (owner), the dispatch gate's "An N-way PANEL… dispatches only on the boss's **explicit go**, never self-authorized" (line 284), THE COUNCIL's "**Consent gates the convening — offered, never auto-fired**" paragraph (428–432), THE COUNCIL's "**When NOT to convene**" paragraph (434–437), COUNCIL SEAT LAW clause 1 ("free is not consent to convene: Gate-0's right-size rule still binds (clause 6)"), and clause 6 ("**A council is still the SPECIAL move.** Consent to spend is not consent to convene"). Six statements of one rule, with a clause in the middle certifying that this is fine.

COST IF WRONG: Nothing — the rule survives in Part I §2 verbatim. The shop notices only if a future editor wonders why the same sentence isn't repeated.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 428–437 (THE COUNCIL: "Consent gates the convening" + "When NOT to convene") and `SPINE.md` COUNCIL SEAT LAW clause 6** — the four downstream echoes of the above

Clause 6 restates clause 1's own tail four clauses later, and they cross-reference each other in a circle.

COST IF WRONG: A reader who jumps straight to THE COUNCIL section without Part I might self-authorize a panel. Mitigated: nothing reaches THE COUNCIL section without loading Part I — SPINE is loaded whole, in order, every summon. ~10 lines.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 466–474 — the entire "### The three flips" section**

EVIDENCE: Four sentences, and every one is either shop history or already law elsewhere. "The builder seat **has flipped** for three causes" is a past-tense account of this shop, not an instruction. The three causes are already in the Builder role definition (line 152: *"Floats between seats per mission (three flips, three causes: capability, price, infrastructure)"*). "The only fixed point is that the lineage which produced the work does not approve it" is the fifth restatement of Principle 3. **[DELETE] `SKILL.md` lines 79–90 — the body of ON INVOCATION step 2**

EVIDENCE: `SKILL.md` line 36 states its own law: *"Every mechanic — dispatch, review, gates, seats, meters, the council — is SPINE's and is already loaded. **This file does not restate it.**"* Step 2 then restates, in ~12 lines, SPINE's entire *Reachability & effective-model preflight* — transport-before-binary, UNKNOWN LINEAGE failing closed, cross-vendor reviewer counting, graceful degradation, unreviewed work never reported done. This is a second copy of law, in the file that forbids second copies, loaded in the same breath as the original. The LEGEND section three paragraphs earlier documents what happens when this file keeps its own copy of something SPINE owns.

What must survive is the *order* — "load `SPINE-WIRING.md`, run SPINE's preflight, declare the arsenal and independence status in one line, then ask for the job." It instructs no one; it explains to a hypothetical confused editor why two numbers differ. The operative line — copy the block verbatim, byte-identical — is already Principle 9's.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 355–372 — the ENDING CREDITS exception and the "Visuals" paragraph**

EVIDENCE: Two separate violations of SPINE's own charter in one section. (a) The ENDING CREDITS clause is **SHOW-tier presentation law living in the character-free engine** — it is carried by "boss amendment, same day" (an attribution scar) and its punchline is *"**The dispatch deck does NOT roll credits**"*, meaning the Deck loads a paragraph every summon to be told a rule that does not apply to it. SPINE's own closing section says wiring lives in `SPINE-WIRING.md` and *"none of it is law."*

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 168–170 — the "claimed atomically" clause inside Part IV's *Bounded***
> *"The cap must be **claimed atomically**, not merely checked: N launches can each read the same free headroom before any of them is recorded, all pass, and together blow the budget. A check that is not a reservation is not a cap."*

EVIDENCE: This is law written to justify the **reservation subsystem the shop deleted this morning**. There is now no reservation anywhere in the harness, so the engine's own text declares that the shop's cap "is not a cap." Code that exists to support something already deleted, in prose form. `dispatch-guard.py`'s live docstring agrees: *"Concurrency is capped by the vendor, or not here."*

COST IF WRONG: A future fleet implementation re-discovers the TOCTOU race. Real risk, but it belongs in whatever builds a fleet, not in the per-summon engine.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 73–75 — Part I §2's "A fleet is legal only if all five hold" bullet**

EVIDENCE: A pointer-plus-copy of Part IV that has **already drifted**: it lists five names (Declared · Bounded · Accounted · still-Principle-3 · Authority-inheritance) while Part IV lists seven bullets, silently dropping *Destined* and *Governed where it RUNS* — and *Governed where it RUNS* is the one clause that covers the vendor-hosted lanes where the actual burn happened. This is the exact failure mode Principle 9 names: "multiple copies is how law forks," demonstrated inside the file that says it.

COST IF WRONG: Gate-0 loses its inline reminder that fleets have a legality test. Part IV is two sections away and unmissable. (Separately worth the owner's eye: line 164, *"A fleet is legal only if all **five** hold:"*, introduces seven bullets — that miscount stays even after this deletion.)

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` line 226 — Part V item 4**
> *"4. **Claims are capped at what a model can prove.** "Gates pass," never "it works." (Ladder of Truth.)"*

EVIDENCE: A numbered clause whose entire content is a quotation of Part I §1 plus a pointer back to it. The same sentence also appears at Mission reports (line 464) and in the canonical invariant block — four times in one load. This one is the purest: it cites its own owner in parentheses.

COST IF WRONG: None. Renumbering Part V is the only work.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 500–503 — "THE EMERGENCY BRAKE (real, rare, quiet)"**

EVIDENCE: This is the BLOCKER rule wearing a second name, three bullets below the BLOCKER rule. Compare triggers — brake: *"correctness rot, data loss, security holes"*; BLOCKER: *"breaks correctness, loses data, bricks the boss's box."* Compare actions — brake: *"write ONE clear report (what breaks, evidence, proposed fix), halt the AFFECTED lane only"*; BLOCKER: *"may surface immediately — WITH a suggested fix,"* and the first bullet already says each stop *"halts the AFFECTED lane only, never the shop."* One rule, two names, and the first bullet's *"**Only two things stop a lane**"* is an artifact of the duplication — there is one.

COST IF WRONG: The pivot instruction (*"pivot the crew to unaffected work"*) is lost here; it survives in Autonomous hours (*"A stoppage is a pivot, not an idle"*). This is one I expected to defend and could not.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 485–487 — "Circle-backs are scheduled, not ambushed"**

EVIDENCE: The bullet immediately above it already says *"Non-blocking reviews land at the CHECKPOINT (lane/episode end)"* and *"what it may not do is halt a builder mid-swing."* This bullet says the same thing in different words: non-blocking findings collect for the checkpoint, no mid-lane ambush. Adjacent restatement, no new mechanism.

COST IF WRONG: None; the rule is intact one line up.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 321–323 — the "Probe the TRANSPORT, not the binary" preflight bullet**

EVIDENCE: The bullet opens by naming its owner — *"(THE TRANSPORT LAW owns this)"* — and then states the rule anyway, in full, including the `--version` caveat. THE TRANSPORT LAW clause 4 says it a second time, and `SKILL.md` step 2 says it a third. Three copies, one of which announces that it is not the owner.

**[DELETE] `SKILL.md` lines 38–39 and lines 53–57**

EVIDENCE: Two separate items in one file. (a) Lines 38–39 repeat lines 34–36 almost word for word — *"The Deck adds NOTHING to the method. Its whole delta is plain rendering"* followed five lines later by *"The Deck adds nothing to the method. Its entire delta is plain rendering + the gold-baton color narration."* The same paragraph twice, back to back, in the file whose thesis is that it doesn't restate things. (b) Lines 53–57 are a dated scar the councils already voted out: *"this file carried a stale v4.0 against SPINE's v4.2 for two days, telling the conductor that purple meant nothing…"* — an incident report inside an instruction. The operative sentence (*"Read THE NOTATION in SPINE and render it plain"*) is the first line and survives.

**[DELETE] `SKILL.md` lines 41–49 — the vendor→color map inside "NARRATE IN COLOR"**

EVIDENCE: This section keeps a private copy of the map (*"🟡➤ conductor … 🟠 Claude · 🔵 Codex · ⚫ Grok · 🟢 Gemini"*) **immediately before** the section that exists to forbid exactly that (*"The Deck does not keep its own copy of the marks"*), in a file that documents having already drifted once from doing this. The multi-line example narration and *"The color is a status light, not a costume"* are illustration, not instruction. The one genuine delta — the gold baton — is stated again at line 59 and survives.

**[DELETE] `SPINE.md` lines 626–630, the "🟣 never means building" clause (632–634), the arrow-etymology sentences (643–646), and the STATES roster (657–659)**

EVIDENCE: THE NOTATION's operative core is small — seat-first, 🔨 build, 🔴/📝 review, ⛔ reject, meter marks mandatory. Around it sits: an orphan `**` on line 626 (a formatting artifact rendering as literal asterisks); version bookkeeping and a dated repeal, *"(v4.0 repealed the 2026-08-09 marks, including 🟣-as-building)"*, plus a second negative-space clause re-stating that repeal; the arrow's origin story, *"The arrow is a **cursor** — that is its birthplace and its meaning"* / *"the arrow's true home"*, which is etymology, not notation; and nine STATES glyphs (🚩 🚧 🧪 🩺 🕵️ 🏁 🚢 🪦 🟤) that no rule anywhere requires an orchestrator to produce. The brief's test is *marks an orchestrator must PRODUCE, not look up* — the STATES roster is a lookup table.

COST IF WRONG: Narration gets less expressive; 🏁 in particular is referenced as the Ladder's top rung, so if it goes, the Ladder's mark goes with it. That one is worth the owner's eye.

---

**[DELETE] `SKILL.md` lines 62–75 — the whole "FUEL MODE" section**

EVIDENCE: Fourteen lines that load on every summon and, by their own declaration, change nothing: *"**Verbiage only.** The register never touches routing, verdicts, evidence rank, tickets, or reports."* It is also off by default and cannot survive a session (*"It is never on unless THIS session's boss turned it on"*), so a stranger downloading the method pays for it every summon and can never have it fire. This is the clearest case in either file of the shop's own preferences billed to everyone who loads the engine.

COST IF WRONG: The boss loses an accommodation he wrote deliberately for himself. **This is a boss call, not a council call** — I flag it because the cost analysis is unambiguous and the value is entirely personal.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/dispatch-guard.py` — `BANNED_STACK` (line 40), the `stacked` block (92–98), the `notes` channel, and the `--max-mode` / `--effort` / `--speed` CLI flags**

EVIDENCE: A guard that cannot guard, verifiable in one line. The only production caller is `wmw_cursor_mcp.py:480` — `rc, problems, _notes = guard.preflight(workdir, model=chosen)` — which passes **no `mode_flags`**, so `flags` is always `{}`, `stacked` is always empty, and the expensive-mode-stack refusal can never fire on a real dispatch. It fires only when a human types the flags into the CLI by hand, i.e. when the human already knows. The same call discards `notes` into `_notes`, so every `notes.append` in `preflight` — including the FAST-tier warning at line 100 — is dead in production too.

COST IF WRONG: The CLI loses a self-audit mode. The empty-repo refusal, which is the check that actually fires, is untouched.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/dispatch-guard.py` docstring lines 7–20, plus `import time` (35), `HOME` (37), and the two orphan section banners (43, 106)**

EVIDENCE: Live dead code and a tombstone. `HOME` lost its only consumer when `STORE` was deleted; `time` is never used (`yield_report` goes through `_now()`); line 43 reads `# ---- locking` above a lone `datetime.now()` wrapper, and line 106 reads `# ---- reservation` above **nothing at all** — a section header for deleted code. The docstring then carries a five-line obituary for that same deleted subsystem (*"A reservation subsystem also lived here and was DELETED 2026-08-24 by a council vote…"*) and attributions (*"Two findings drove this, neither of them mine: Boss — … Kimi — …"*) that the councils already voted out everywhere else.

COST IF WRONG: A future editor rebuilds a reservation subsystem because nothing warns them off. Cheap: the warning belongs in the council record, which already holds it. The *"WHAT THIS CANNOT DO"* paragraph must stay — see DEFEND.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/read-meters.py` line 195 and the `bench-burn.py` reference at line 14**

EVIDENCE: This is a **live defect**, not just bloat. An earlier trim removed the second half of the closing print and left the first half behind, so every non-JSON meter read now ends by printing a truncated sentence to the operator: *"Neither vendor publishes a pool SIZE — only a percentage. To learn the size,"* — and then stops. The remaining docstring line still points at *"`bench-burn.py` reports what a burn cost"*, a file the shop deleted today. Both are references to something already gone.

COST IF WRONG: None. The methodology has its own home — THE METER LAW's own footnote says it lives in `MEASURING-POOLS.md` and is *"not law."*

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/armcheck.py` lines 83–93 — the reserve-path canary**

EVIDENCE: Its comment states its purpose: *"This canary exercises the reserve path itself"* and *"the ONLY test that reaches the reserve path."* **The reserve path was deleted this morning.** The check it prints — `"cursor: the guarded write path RUNS (no NameError in reserve)"` — asserts the absence of a NameError in code that no longer exists, and under `--deep` it **spends a real dispatch** to do it. A test that costs money to prove something about deleted code.

COST IF WRONG: `--deep` loses its only live write-path smoke test. If the shop wants that coverage it should be re-aimed at the preflight path, but as written it is paying tokens for a null assertion.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/wmw_cursor_mcp.py` — `COUNCIL_LOCK_ON` (line 72) and the boss-ruling narration in its refusal message (lines 449–459)**

EVIDENCE: The council lock no longer has bounds of its own — line 447 reads `if recent >= _allowance_calls("cursor", COUNCIL_LOCK_MAX)` against `_allowance_window_s(...)`, i.e. it now enforces **the operator's allowance record**, and `_allowance("cursor")` has already refused the call fifteen lines earlier if no grant exists. What remains unique is the branding and an env-var (`WMW_CURSOR_COUNCIL_LOCK=off`) whose only function is to **silently disable enforcement of the operator's own granted bound** — a switch that turns off the allowance while the allowance record still reads as granted. The refusal text then narrates a dated boss ruling and lists council seats, which is doctrine in a runtime error message.

COST IF WRONG: The escape hatch is gone, so a legitimately-needed burst requires re-granting a wider allowance — which is exactly what COUNCIL SEAT LAW clause 4 demands (*"Widening a bound is a fresh decision, made out loud"*). Deleting the switch makes the code match the law.

---

**[DELETE] `mcp-seats/wmw_cursor_mcp.py` `_safe_cwd` — the secret-directory loop (packet lines 369–373)**
> `for secret in (".ssh", ".aws", ".grok", ".gemini", ".claude", ".cursor", ".config", ".azure", ".kube", ".gnupg")`

EVIDENCE: The brief asks which controls are ceremony, and this is the clearest one. **`cwd` is not a jail.** A `--yolo` agent rooted at `C:\Sync\Projects\foo` can write `~/.ssh/id_rsa` with an absolute path; nothing here prevents it. This loop blocks only the case where the *caller deliberately points `cwd` at* `~/.ssh` — a typo, not an adversary. It is sold as security (the neighbouring APPDATA block cites *"a write-capable session rooted there can rewrite the very tools that enforce these guards"*), which is the false assurance the audit named: every control here runs with the same authority as what it claims to stop. `armcheck.py` then spends four canaries testing this boundary.

COST IF WRONG: A fat-fingered `cwd` into a credential directory stops being caught. Honest accounting: the loop is real typo-prevention and near-free — but it must not be *counted* as a fence, and the tests that dress it as one are the ceremony. **I would delete the loop only if the shop is willing to stop calling `cwd` a boundary; otherwise delete the claim, not the code.** Flagging rather than voting hard.

---

# DEFEND — what must NOT go

- **Principle 3, Part IV's anti-laundering guard (*"a name is not a lineage"*), and the effective-model preflight.** This is the entire reason the method exists. The clause that a host *"can rent another vendor's brain"* is the one thing standing between the shop and a review that is a model approving itself. It reads as long; it is the load-bearing wall.
- **Part V §5, the three lists and the containment rule.** `actual delta ⊆ write set` and `actual delta ⊆ review manifest`, with the reviewer computing its own hashes. It is the only mechanism anywhere that catches a builder curating what its reviewer sees. Independence of identity is worthless without it, and nothing else in the engine does this job.
- **The Ladder's oracle check and the RED-first rule** — *"An untested test is an opinion with a green checkmark."* Delete this and green gates start meaning "shipped."
- **"Ambiguity is a finding, never an input"** and the builder-ticket line *"I could not tell what you meant is a good outcome."* The scar attached to it is deletable; the instruction is the cheapest defect-prevention in the file.
- **Gate-0's dispatch gate and the right-size default** (*"Both no → just do it"*, one builder + one reviewer as canon). This clause *is* the lean-mean-machine standard the owner stated. Cutting the engine while cutting this would be self-defeating.
- **Principle 10** — the boss is on a phone, a blocked seat re-plans instead of handing the block back. It is the difference between an orchestrator and a very expensive to-do list.
- **The whole prompt-spill transport in `wmw_cursor_mcp.py`**, `_MODEL_RE`, `_UUID_RE`, and `--mode ask` over bare `--trust`. Not ceremony — a reproduced command-injection on this machine, and a v1.0 "read-only" call that wrote a file. This is the harness's one honest, evidence-backed control.
- **`_guard()` failing closed and the `GUARD UNAVAILABLE` refusal.** A control that vanishes when its file breaks is not a control; this is the fix, and it must not be re-simplified away.
- **The credit guard, `UNKNOWN`-fails-closed (including `auto`), the allowance record, and mandatory meter marks on any line that can spend.** For a stranger downloading this method, these four are the only thing between them and a bill. They are the literal answer to *"I don't want people to… find out they burned all of their usage from our setup."*
- **`preflight`'s empty-repo / no-source refusal, and `dispatch-guard.py`'s "WHAT THIS CANNOT DO" paragraph.** The first is the only control aimed at the burn that actually happened. The second is the most valuable prose in the codebase: a control that states plainly what it does not govern is worth more than one that lets you assume.

---

# THE ONE THING

**`SPINE.md` lines 66–68 — the clause that licenses deliberate restatement.**

It is the only sentence in the engine that *authorizes* saying a rule more than once, it justifies itself by citing the Amendment Law, and **the Amendment Law was deleted this morning**. So it is simultaneously the cause of the largest duplication in the file (one rule, six statements) and a dead reference. Every other entry on my list removes an instance of the disease; this one removes the prescription. Delete it and the four downstream echoes have no defense left; leave it and the next editor has written permission to re-add them.

---

# CONFIDENCE

**High** on the mechanical findings, which are checkable in seconds and do not depend on my judgment: the Amendment Law citation, the "five holds" over a seven-item list, the `# ---- reservation` banner above nothing, `HOME` and `import time` orphaned, `BANNED_STACK` unreachable from its only production caller, `_notes` discarded, the truncated sentence `read-meters.py` now prints to the operator, the reserve canary spending a live dispatch on deleted code, and `SKILL.md` stating "this file does not restate it" forty lines above a full restatement of SPINE's preflight. Any seat can verify all of those, and any that disagrees is simply wrong.

**Medium** on THE NOTATION and the ENDING CREDITS/Visuals block. My reasoning is sound but these are the owner's voice, and voice is his call, not a council's.

**Deliberately flagged rather than voted:** FUEL MODE (personal accommodation, unambiguous cost, value only he can price) and the `_safe_cwd` secret-directory loop (where my honest read is that the *claim* is the problem, not the code).

**On my standing:** I am a labeled degraded self-check, same lineage as the author, no memory of the day that produced this. Per the brief, my agreements are weak evidence — so discount everywhere I merely re-found what four councils already agreed on. The places I felt the pull to approve and did not are these four, and I would weight them accordingly: **the emergency brake is the BLOCKER rule under a second name** (I expected to defend it), **the `notes` channel and mode-stack guard are dead in production** (they look like working controls and are not), **`SKILL.md` keeps a forked copy of the color map in the section immediately preceding the one forbidding forked copies**, and **the consent gate is stated six times under a clause certifying that this is correct**. That last one is where a fresh reader's advantage is real: the author could see the clause and read it as a decision; with no investment in it, it reads as the bug.

seat never answered - attack never landed"`. A guard test that passes when the attack never landed is worse than no test; this is the correction, not the ceremony.
- **Principle 1's `a signature identifies the **declared** seat, not a verified model`** and `The signature makes identity **legible and falsifiable**, not proven.` Given that an audit already called this harness false assurance, the honest labeling of a control's limits is the most valuable prose in Part III. Deleting it converts a legible control into a claimed one.
- **`**Review coverage is never the thing you cut**`** — the survivor of item 16's third bullet.
- **Principle 10 and phone-readable mission reports.** The method's user is on a phone; a rule that keeps plans from silently requiring his hands is load-bearing, not courtesy.

---

# THE ONE THING

**THE NOTATION's decorative and archaeological half (item 2).**

If I get one delete, I take the largest block of text in the per-summon path that no decision depends on. Nothing in dispatch, routing, review, adjudication, or metering branches on `🪦`, `🟤`, `🕵️`, `🎼`, or on the etymology of an arrow. It is a glyph dictionary in a section whose own charter says it is not a lookup, it carries repealed-mark history that exists only to describe what a mark no longer means, it holds per-pool vendor wiring that SPINE says lives in `SPINE-WIRING.md` and that the seat wrapper already computes and prints itself, and it teaches the Deck the crew-color grammar of a tier the Deck refuses to load.

I chose it because it is the item I felt the strongest pull to approve. It is the shop's handwriting — it is fun, it is identity, and four councils in one day left it alone while cutting laws. That is exactly the signature the brief sent me to look for: not a rule anybody defended, a block nobody examined.

---

# CONFIDENCE

**High** on items 4, 9, 10, 11, and 13 — these are checkable facts, not judgments. I verified each against the packet: `MAX_CONCURRENT`, `LEASE_TTL_MIN`, `LOCK_STALE_S`, `MAX_SINGLE_CLAIM_PCT`, `MAX_OUTSTANDING_PCT`, `STORE`, `LOCK`, `import time` and `RESV` have no readers; the reserve path the `--deep` canary tests is absent from the guard block it points at; `bench-burn.py` is on your own deleted list and is printed to stdout on every meter read; Part IV lists seven terms under the words "all five" and the Part I summary drops the two that cost money; the "Deck adds nothing" sentence appears twice in one paragraph.

**High** on items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 as *duplication and description*; **medium** on whether you want them gone. Item 3 has a structural argument I would press: its own justification cites the Amendment Law, which you deleted this morning, so the clause authorizing the redundancy no longer has a law behind it.

**Medium** on 12, 14, 15, and 16. Item 12 needs the split I named — reasons stay, dates and finder credits go — and I would not want a mechanical purge to take the *why-nots* with them.

**Low, and deliberately submitted anyway** on 17. Under your decision rule a single vote changes nothing, and this is the one file in the packet that spends a stranger's month by design, so it should be on the record even if it stays.

**On my standing:** I am a labeled degraded self-check, same lineage as the author, and I found the pull to approve concentrated in exactly three places — THE NOTATION, THE COUNCIL, and FUEL MODE. All three are identity rather than method, and I named all three. Where I agreed with the existing text, that is weak evidence and I have said so in the DEFEND section rather than pretending it is independent confirmation. Two places I checked expecting to find ceremony and found a real guard instead — `_safe_cwd`'s secret list and the prompt spill transport — are reported as defends, not deletes.
